**World Taekwondo** (**WT**), formerly the **World Taekwondo Federation** (**WTF**), is an international federation governing the sport of [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo") and [para taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para_taekwondo "Para taekwondo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-2) WT is a member of the [Association of Summer Olympic International Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Summer_Olympic_International_Federations "Association of Summer Olympic International Federations") (ASOIF).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-3)

The World Taekwondo Federation was established on 28 May 1973, at its inaugural meeting held at the [Kukkiwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kukkiwon "Kukkiwon") with participation of 35 representatives from around the world. As of May 2023[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit) there are 213 member nations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-elects-4) Since 2004, Choue Chung-won has been the president of World Taekwondo, succeeding the first president, [Kim Un-yong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Un-yong "Kim Un-yong").

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Flags_Kukkiwon_Seoul.JPG/250px-Flags_Kukkiwon_Seoul.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flags_Kukkiwon_Seoul.JPG)

Flagpoles and flags of the World Taekwondo and of the Korean Taekwondo Association at the [Kukkiwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kukkiwon "Kukkiwon") in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea

World Taekwondo was recognized by the [International Paralympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Paralympic_Committee "International Paralympic Committee") (IPC) on October 16, 2013, and the IPC later included taekwondo in the Tokyo [2020 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Paralympics "2020 Summer Paralympics"). On 17 July 1980, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) recognized the World Taekwondo Federation at its 83rd Session in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), Russia. Taekwondo debuted as a demonstration sport of the [1988 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea. On 4 September 1994, Taekwondo was adopted as an official sport of the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") at the 103rd IOC Session in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_intro-5)

In June 2017, the World Taekwondo Federation was renamed as World Taekwondo to avoid its acronym clashing with the common Internet slang [WTF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTF_(Internet_slang) "WTF (Internet slang)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-8)

## Organizational structure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Organizational structure")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/9a/World_Taekwondo_Federation_old_logo.svg/250px-World_Taekwondo_Federation_old_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:World_Taekwondo_Federation_old_logo.svg)

Old WTF logo

The main constituents of World Taekwondo are the following: The General Assembly (GA); the World Taekwondo Council; the President and the Secretariat. In addition to its main constituents World Taekwondo also encompasses other organizations that have been duly authorized or recognized by the Council and the GA and that operate under the auspices of World Taekwondo.

World Taekwondo-recognized or authorized organizations include but are not limited to the Continental Unions. The General Assembly is the general meeting of the council and representatives of MNAs of World Taekwondo. The GA is World Taekwondo's supreme decision making organ. Its decisions are final, whereas the Council consists of the President, the Vice Presidents, the Secretary General, the Treasurer and the Council members. Responsibilities of the council are for example planning and management of World Taekwondo organization and operations and the control over the financial budget and financial reports. The President is elected by the GA from among its members for a term of four years. The President must lead and represent World Taekwondo; concurrently lead the GA and the council as its chairman, and preside over meetings and other activities as well as designate official duties to Vice Presidents on an ad-hoc basis for the betterment of the development of the sport of taekwondo and World Taekwondo operations. Furthermore, the President appoints the chairmen and members of World Taekwondo Committees. Lastly, the Secretariat of World Taekwondo is installed at the location of World Taekwondo headquarters for the execution of the secretarial affairs and duties of the President and the Secretary General.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_Organizational_Structure_2-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_Organizational_Structure-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The World Taekwondo Federation (WTF) was established on May 28, 1973, at the inaugural meeting held at the Kukkiwon with participation of 35 representatives from the world after it separated from the [International Taekwon-Do Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Taekwon-Do_Federation "International Taekwon-Do Federation") because of political reasons. At that time, [Un Yong Kim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un_Yong_Kim "Un Yong Kim") was elected president for a four-year term. One of the main Constituents of World Taekwondo, the Secretariat was formed on June 3, 1973, and began operating.

On October 8, 1974, World Taekwondo was affiliated to the General Association of International Sports Federations (GAISF), now SportAccord. Until the 1980s, the European (May, 1976), the Asian (October, 1976), the Pan American (September, 1978) and the African (April, 1979) Taekwondo Unions inaugural meetings were held, while Oceania's Taekwondo Union was not recognized as the 5th Continental Union of World Taekwondo until July 16, 2005.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-11)

The recognition of the IOC towards World Taekwondo at its 83rd session in Moscow on July 17, 1980, was the cornerstone for their Cooperation. Thereupon Taekwondo participated in the 24th Olympiad at Changchung Gymnasium in Seoul, Korea as well as the [25th Olympiad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") at the Palau Blaugrana in Barcelona, Spain as a demonstration sport.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-12)

In recognition of his contribution to the Olympic Movement Un Yong Kim was awarded the Order of Commander by Prince Rainier of Monaco on September 21, 1993. Moreover, Taekwondo was adopted as an official sport of the 2000 Summer Olympics at the 103rd IOC session in Paris, France, on September 4, 1994. Half a year later, on February 15, 1995, World Taekwondo was affiliated with the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations (ASOIF) as a provisional member.

After the first appearance of Taekwondo as an Olympic Sport in the 2000 Summer Olympics, the IOC executive board confirms Taekwondo as an Olympic Sport for the 2004 Summer Olympics on December 11–13, 2000. Furthermore, the inclusion of taekwondo in the 2008 Summer Olympics was confirmed on November 29, 2002, at the 114th IOC session held in Mexico City.

On February 15, 2004, the Vice President (Italy) Sun Jae Park was elected as Acting President of World Taekwondo due to the resignation of the founding President Un Yong Kim from the presidency of World Taekwondo. Four month later Chung Won Choue was elected as new President of World Taekwondo at the extraordinary General Assembly on June 11, 2004. Taekwondo was confirmed as program of the 2012 Summer Olympics on July 8, 2005.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_History-13)

In June 2017, the body was renamed World Taekwondo to avoid the "negative connotations" of the acronym associated with the common [Internet slang WTF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTF_(Internet_slang) "WTF (Internet slang)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-15)

## Mission and objectives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mission and objectives")]

The mission of World Taekwondo is to provide effective international governance of taekwondo as an Olympic sport and Paralympic sport. The envisioned objectives of World Taekwondo are to promote, expand, and improve worldwide the practice of taekwondo in light of its educational, cultural, and sports values (the "Taekwondo movement") and to promote fair play, youth development, and education as well as to encourage peace and cooperation though participation in sports. Moreover, World Taekwondo wants to promote or sanction international taekwondo competitions and relating to those World Taekwondo resolves to constantly improve technical rules regulating taekwondo competitions and poomsae competitions sanctioned or promoted by World Taekwondo, including the taekwondo event of the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games. Furthermore, World Taekwondo wants to take action in order to strengthen the unity and protect the interests of World Taekwondo and the Taekwondo Movement as well as to engage in other activities in support of the above objectives. World Taekwondo undertakes its missions and objectives in cooperation with independent affiliated organizations including World Taekwondo Academy, World Taekwondo Peace Corps, World Taekwondo Demonstration Team, Pro Taekwondo Federation, Global Taekwondo Support Federation, and Taekwondo International Federation.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_M&O-16)

**World Taekwondo** (**WT**), formerly the **World Taekwondo Federation** (**WTF**), is an international federation governing the sport of [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo") and [para taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para_taekwondo "Para taekwondo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-2) WT is a member of the [Association of Summer Olympic International Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Summer_Olympic_International_Federations "Association of Summer Olympic International Federations") (ASOIF).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-3)

The World Taekwondo Federation was established on 28 May 1973, at its inaugural meeting held at the [Kukkiwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kukkiwon "Kukkiwon") with participation of 35 representatives from around the world. As of May 2023[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit) there are 213 member nations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-elects-4) Since 2004, Choue Chung-won has been the president of World Taekwondo, succeeding the first president, [Kim Un-yong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Un-yong "Kim Un-yong").

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Flags_Kukkiwon_Seoul.JPG/250px-Flags_Kukkiwon_Seoul.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flags_Kukkiwon_Seoul.JPG)

Flagpoles and flags of the World Taekwondo and of the Korean Taekwondo Association at the [Kukkiwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kukkiwon "Kukkiwon") in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea

World Taekwondo was recognized by the [International Paralympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Paralympic_Committee "International Paralympic Committee") (IPC) on October 16, 2013, and the IPC later included taekwondo in the Tokyo [2020 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Paralympics "2020 Summer Paralympics"). On 17 July 1980, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) recognized the World Taekwondo Federation at its 83rd Session in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), Russia. Taekwondo debuted as a demonstration sport of the [1988 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea. On 4 September 1994, Taekwondo was adopted as an official sport of the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") at the 103rd IOC Session in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_intro-5)

In June 2017, the World Taekwondo Federation was renamed as World Taekwondo to avoid its acronym clashing with the common Internet slang [WTF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTF_(Internet_slang) "WTF (Internet slang)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-8)

## Organizational structure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Organizational structure")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/9a/World_Taekwondo_Federation_old_logo.svg/250px-World_Taekwondo_Federation_old_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:World_Taekwondo_Federation_old_logo.svg)

Old WTF logo

The main constituents of World Taekwondo are the following: The General Assembly (GA); the World Taekwondo Council; the President and the Secretariat. In addition to its main constituents World Taekwondo also encompasses other organizations that have been duly authorized or recognized by the Council and the GA and that operate under the auspices of World Taekwondo.

World Taekwondo-recognized or authorized organizations include but are not limited to the Continental Unions. The General Assembly is the general meeting of the council and representatives of MNAs of World Taekwondo. The GA is World Taekwondo's supreme decision making organ. Its decisions are final, whereas the Council consists of the President, the Vice Presidents, the Secretary General, the Treasurer and the Council members. Responsibilities of the council are for example planning and management of World Taekwondo organization and operations and the control over the financial budget and financial reports. The President is elected by the GA from among its members for a term of four years. The President must lead and represent World Taekwondo; concurrently lead the GA and the council as its chairman, and preside over meetings and other activities as well as designate official duties to Vice Presidents on an ad-hoc basis for the betterment of the development of the sport of taekwondo and World Taekwondo operations. Furthermore, the President appoints the chairmen and members of World Taekwondo Committees. Lastly, the Secretariat of World Taekwondo is installed at the location of World Taekwondo headquarters for the execution of the secretarial affairs and duties of the President and the Secretary General.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_Organizational_Structure_2-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_Organizational_Structure-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The World Taekwondo Federation (WTF) was established on May 28, 1973, at the inaugural meeting held at the Kukkiwon with participation of 35 representatives from the world after it separated from the [International Taekwon-Do Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Taekwon-Do_Federation "International Taekwon-Do Federation") because of political reasons. At that time, [Un Yong Kim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un_Yong_Kim "Un Yong Kim") was elected president for a four-year term. One of the main Constituents of World Taekwondo, the Secretariat was formed on June 3, 1973, and began operating.

On October 8, 1974, World Taekwondo was affiliated to the General Association of International Sports Federations (GAISF), now SportAccord. Until the 1980s, the European (May, 1976), the Asian (October, 1976), the Pan American (September, 1978) and the African (April, 1979) Taekwondo Unions inaugural meetings were held, while Oceania's Taekwondo Union was not recognized as the 5th Continental Union of World Taekwondo until July 16, 2005.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-11)

The recognition of the IOC towards World Taekwondo at its 83rd session in Moscow on July 17, 1980, was the cornerstone for their Cooperation. Thereupon Taekwondo participated in the 24th Olympiad at Changchung Gymnasium in Seoul, Korea as well as the [25th Olympiad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") at the Palau Blaugrana in Barcelona, Spain as a demonstration sport.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-12)

In recognition of his contribution to the Olympic Movement Un Yong Kim was awarded the Order of Commander by Prince Rainier of Monaco on September 21, 1993. Moreover, Taekwondo was adopted as an official sport of the 2000 Summer Olympics at the 103rd IOC session in Paris, France, on September 4, 1994. Half a year later, on February 15, 1995, World Taekwondo was affiliated with the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations (ASOIF) as a provisional member.

After the first appearance of Taekwondo as an Olympic Sport in the 2000 Summer Olympics, the IOC executive board confirms Taekwondo as an Olympic Sport for the 2004 Summer Olympics on December 11–13, 2000. Furthermore, the inclusion of taekwondo in the 2008 Summer Olympics was confirmed on November 29, 2002, at the 114th IOC session held in Mexico City.

On February 15, 2004, the Vice President (Italy) Sun Jae Park was elected as Acting President of World Taekwondo due to the resignation of the founding President Un Yong Kim from the presidency of World Taekwondo. Four month later Chung Won Choue was elected as new President of World Taekwondo at the extraordinary General Assembly on June 11, 2004. Taekwondo was confirmed as program of the 2012 Summer Olympics on July 8, 2005.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_History-13)

In June 2017, the body was renamed World Taekwondo to avoid the "negative connotations" of the acronym associated with the common [Internet slang WTF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTF_(Internet_slang) "WTF (Internet slang)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-15)

## Mission and objectives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mission and objectives")]

The mission of World Taekwondo is to provide effective international governance of taekwondo as an Olympic sport and Paralympic sport. The envisioned objectives of World Taekwondo are to promote, expand, and improve worldwide the practice of taekwondo in light of its educational, cultural, and sports values (the "Taekwondo movement") and to promote fair play, youth development, and education as well as to encourage peace and cooperation though participation in sports. Moreover, World Taekwondo wants to promote or sanction international taekwondo competitions and relating to those World Taekwondo resolves to constantly improve technical rules regulating taekwondo competitions and poomsae competitions sanctioned or promoted by World Taekwondo, including the taekwondo event of the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games. Furthermore, World Taekwondo wants to take action in order to strengthen the unity and protect the interests of World Taekwondo and the Taekwondo Movement as well as to engage in other activities in support of the above objectives. World Taekwondo undertakes its missions and objectives in cooperation with independent affiliated organizations including World Taekwondo Academy, World Taekwondo Peace Corps, World Taekwondo Demonstration Team, Pro Taekwondo Federation, Global Taekwondo Support Federation, and Taekwondo International Federation.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-WTF_M&O-16)

## Membership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Membership")]

As of 2026, the global membership of World Taekwondo stands at 215 national member associations (NMAs, 214 active and 1 suspended), spanning five Continental Unions (CUs).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo_Federation#cite_note-elects-4)

### Continental Unions (CUs)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Taekwondo&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Continental Unions (CUs)")]

*   [African Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Taekwondo_Union "African Taekwondo Union") (AFTU) – 54 national member associations
*   [Asian Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Taekwondo_Union "Asian Taekwondo Union") (ATU) – 44 national member associations
*   [European Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Taekwondo_Union "European Taekwondo Union") (ETU) – 52 national member associations
*   [Oceania Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania_Taekwondo_Union "Oceania Taekwondo Union") (OTU) – 19 member national associations
*   [Pan American Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan_American_Taekwondo_Union "Pan American Taekwondo Union") (PATU) – 46 national member associations

The **World Karate Federation** (**WKF**) is an international governing body of [sport karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_karate "Sport karate") with 198 member countries.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-4) It is the only karate organization recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") and has more than a hundred million members.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-8) The WKF organizes their Junior and Senior [Karate World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_World_Championships "Karate World Championships"), which are each held every other year. WKF is recognised member of the [International World Games Association (IWGA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_World_Games_Association "International World Games Association"), as the governing body for karate in the [World Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Games "World Games")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-9) The President of the WKF is [Antonio Espinós](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Espin%C3%B3s "Antonio Espinós"), and the headquarters are located in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Karate_Federation&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate") was introduced to [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") around the 1950s by [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_people "Japanese people")[masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_(athletics) "Masters (athletics)"), mainly from the [Japan Karate Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Karate_Association "Japan Karate Association") (JKA).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-BBF76-11) In 1961, Jacques Delcourt was appointed President of [French Karate Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Karate_Federation "French Karate Federation"), which was at that stage an associated member of the [French Judo Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Judo_Federation "French Judo Federation"). In 1963 he invited the six other known European federations ([Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain"), [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain")) to come to France for the first-ever international karate event, and Great Britain and Belgium accepted the invitation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-google288-12)

In December of that year, six of the seven federations gathered in Paris, in what was to be the first European Karate Congress, with the aim of improving and organising karate tournaments between their countries. It was noted that the unification of the different karate styles was impossible, and so they decided to unify the refereeing.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-google288-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-13)

By 1963 the [European Karate Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Karate_Federation "European Karate Federation") was created, with [Jacques Delcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Delcourt "Jacques Delcourt") voted in as President. The following year the first European Karate Championships were held, in Paris.

In 1970, the International Karate Union (IKU) was formed by [Jacques Delcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Delcourt "Jacques Delcourt") in an effort to organise karate at the world level. Upon hearing this, [Ryoichi Sasakawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryoichi_Sasakawa "Ryoichi Sasakawa"), President of the [Federation of All Japan Karatedo Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_All_Japan_Karatedo_Organization "Federation of All Japan Karatedo Organization") (FAJKO), which later changed its name to the [Japan Karate Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Karate_Federation "Japan Karate Federation") (JKF), travelled to France to discuss the creation of an international governing body.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-BBF76-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-14) The IKU was quickly disbanded and a new organisation was formed between the EKU and the Japanese federation, and was called the World Union of Karate-do Organizations (WUKO).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-Evans1988-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-16)

In 1985 the World Union of Karate-do Organizations was officially recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") as the official board for karate.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-17)

The integration of several new organizations during the 1990s saw WUKO membership increase to 150 National Federations. Therefore, a new name that would more accurately reflect the size and scope of the organization was needed. The name of the first International organization representing sport Karate was thus changed to World Karate Federation (WKF) on December 20, 1992.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-18)

The significant growth of WKF resulted in a consolidated organisation that fully represented the sport of Karate at the international level. This legitimacy was confirmed in 1999 when the IOC officially recognised the World Karate Federation as the sole governing body for the sport of Karate in the world. [[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-19)

In August 2016 it was announced [Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Karate at the Summer Olympics") would be in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-21)

## Members

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Karate_Federation&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Members")]

The global membership of the World Karate Federation stands at 200 national federation members, spanning five continents.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-WKF_Members-22)

### Guardian Girls Karate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Karate_Federation&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Guardian Girls Karate")]

[Guardian Girls Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian_Girls_International "Guardian Girls International") (GGK) is a global project originally developed by the [Koyamada International Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koyamada_International_Foundation "Koyamada International Foundation") (KIF) and later transferred to [Guardian Girls International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian_Girls_International "Guardian Girls International"). Launched in partnership with the WKF and [UNFPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNFPA "UNFPA") in October 2022 in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), the project has been licensed to WKF since 2024 and is administered exclusively by the WKF and implemented locally through WKF’s authorized national federation members worldwide, in collaboration with GGI and KIF’s national chapters.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-31)

The **World Karate Federation** (**WKF**) is an international governing body of [sport karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_karate "Sport karate") with 198 member countries.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-4) It is the only karate organization recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") and has more than a hundred million members.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-8) The WKF organizes their Junior and Senior [Karate World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_World_Championships "Karate World Championships"), which are each held every other year. WKF is recognised member of the [International World Games Association (IWGA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_World_Games_Association "International World Games Association"), as the governing body for karate in the [World Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Games "World Games")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-9) The President of the WKF is [Antonio Espinós](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Espin%C3%B3s "Antonio Espinós"), and the headquarters are located in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Karate_Federation&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate") was introduced to [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") around the 1950s by [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_people "Japanese people")[masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_(athletics) "Masters (athletics)"), mainly from the [Japan Karate Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Karate_Association "Japan Karate Association") (JKA).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-BBF76-11) In 1961, Jacques Delcourt was appointed President of [French Karate Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Karate_Federation "French Karate Federation"), which was at that stage an associated member of the [French Judo Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Judo_Federation "French Judo Federation"). In 1963 he invited the six other known European federations ([Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain"), [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain")) to come to France for the first-ever international karate event, and Great Britain and Belgium accepted the invitation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-google288-12)

In December of that year, six of the seven federations gathered in Paris, in what was to be the first European Karate Congress, with the aim of improving and organising karate tournaments between their countries. It was noted that the unification of the different karate styles was impossible, and so they decided to unify the refereeing.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-google288-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-13)

By 1963 the [European Karate Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Karate_Federation "European Karate Federation") was created, with [Jacques Delcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Delcourt "Jacques Delcourt") voted in as President. The following year the first European Karate Championships were held, in Paris.

In 1970, the International Karate Union (IKU) was formed by [Jacques Delcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Delcourt "Jacques Delcourt") in an effort to organise karate at the world level. Upon hearing this, [Ryoichi Sasakawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryoichi_Sasakawa "Ryoichi Sasakawa"), President of the [Federation of All Japan Karatedo Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_All_Japan_Karatedo_Organization "Federation of All Japan Karatedo Organization") (FAJKO), which later changed its name to the [Japan Karate Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Karate_Federation "Japan Karate Federation") (JKF), travelled to France to discuss the creation of an international governing body.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-BBF76-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-14) The IKU was quickly disbanded and a new organisation was formed between the EKU and the Japanese federation, and was called the World Union of Karate-do Organizations (WUKO).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-Evans1988-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-16)

In 1985 the World Union of Karate-do Organizations was officially recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") as the official board for karate.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-17)

The integration of several new organizations during the 1990s saw WUKO membership increase to 150 National Federations. Therefore, a new name that would more accurately reflect the size and scope of the organization was needed. The name of the first International organization representing sport Karate was thus changed to World Karate Federation (WKF) on December 20, 1992.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-18)

The significant growth of WKF resulted in a consolidated organisation that fully represented the sport of Karate at the international level. This legitimacy was confirmed in 1999 when the IOC officially recognised the World Karate Federation as the sole governing body for the sport of Karate in the world. [[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-19)

In August 2016 it was announced [Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Karate at the Summer Olympics") would be in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-21)

### Guardian Girls Karate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Karate_Federation&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Guardian Girls Karate")]

[Guardian Girls Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian_Girls_International "Guardian Girls International") (GGK) is a global project originally developed by the [Koyamada International Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koyamada_International_Foundation "Koyamada International Foundation") (KIF) and later transferred to [Guardian Girls International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian_Girls_International "Guardian Girls International"). Launched in partnership with the WKF and [UNFPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNFPA "UNFPA") in October 2022 in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), the project has been licensed to WKF since 2024 and is administered exclusively by the WKF and implemented locally through WKF’s authorized national federation members worldwide, in collaboration with GGI and KIF’s national chapters.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Federation#cite_note-31)

[Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate") was an event held in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan. It was the debut appearance of [karate at the Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Karate at the Summer Olympics"). Karate was one of four optional sports added to the Olympic program specifically for 2020,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-1) rather than as a permanent sport.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-3) After it was announced it would not be included in 2024, in August 2022 it was announced that karate had made the shortlist for inclusion in the [2028 Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics "2028 Summer Olympics"), although it was ultimately not selected.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-5)

The karate competitions at the 2020 Olympics featured eight events.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Tokyo_2020_Karate-6) Two karate disciplines were featured: [kumite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumite "Kumite") was the sparring discipline and had three weight classes each for men and women; [kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kata_(martial_arts) "Kata (martial arts)") was the solo form discipline, and had one event each for men and women. Competitors chose the kata to demonstrate from 102 kata that were recognized by the World Karate Federation. Competitors were not allowed to demonstrate the same kata twice during the tournament.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Tokyo_2020_Karate-6) Each event had 10 competitors.

The three weight classes in Olympic competition for kumite were in contrast to the five normally used by the World Karate Federation (WKF). The two lightest (-60 kg and -67 kg for men, -50 kg and -55 kg for women) were combined into the Olympic categories of -67 kg for men and -55 kg for women. The middle categories (-75 kg men, -61 kg women) were unchanged, while the two heaviest categories (-84 kg and +84 kg for men, -68 kg and +68 kg for women) were combined into +75 kg for men and +61 kg for women.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

The effort to bring karate to the Olympics was begun in the 1970s by [Jacques Delcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Delcourt "Jacques Delcourt").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Inc.1985-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Coleman1993-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-9) In 2009, in the [121st International Olympic Committee voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/121st_IOC_Session "121st IOC Session"), karate did not receive the necessary two-thirds majority vote to become an [Olympic sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sport "Olympic sport").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-10) Karate was being considered for the 2020 Olympics;[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-11) however, at a meeting of the IOC's executive board, held in [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") on 29 May 2013, it was decided that karate (along with [wushu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wushu_(sport) "Wushu (sport)") and several other sports) would not be considered for inclusion in 2020 at the [IOC's 125th session](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/125th_IOC_Session "125th IOC Session") in [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), in September 2013.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-12)

In September 2015, karate was included in a shortlist with [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Baseball at the Summer Olympics"), [softball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Softball at the Summer Olympics"), [skateboarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skateboarding_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Skateboarding at the Summer Olympics"), [surfing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Surfing at the Summer Olympics"), and [sport climbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_climbing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Sport climbing at the Summer Olympics") to be considered for inclusion in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-13) and in June 2016, the Executive Board of the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) announced that they would support the proposal to include all of the shortlisted sports in the 2020 Games.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-14) Finally, on 3 August 2016, all five sports (counting baseball and softball together as one sport) were approved for inclusion in the 2020 Olympic program.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-15) Karate will not be included in the [2024 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Olympic_Games "2024 Olympic Games") or the 2028 Games.

## Rules

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Rules")]

For both kumite and kata, WKF rules, effective as of January 2018, have been adopted.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17) In January 2019, a point-based system was adopted for kata.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:1-18)

### Kumite

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Kumite")]

The individual tournament for the Kumite competition at the World Karate Federation (WKF) [Karate World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_World_Championships "Karate World Championships") is held under a weight class system comprising five divisions each for both men and women.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-19) However, the Kumite competition at the Summer Olympics consisted of just three divisions each, thus:

*   Weight classes for men: −67 kg, −75 kg, +75 kg
*   Weight classes for women: −55 kg, −61 kg, +61 kg[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-20)

Two competitors face each other in a matted competition area of 8 m ×8 m (26 ft ×26 ft). Each match is competed for 3 minutes, unless one competitor amasses eight points more than their opponent.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:1-18) A competitor wins by amassing eight points more than their opponent or by gaining more points than their opponent in the allotted time of 3 minutes. In the event of a tie, the competitor who scored the first point is the winner. In the case of a scoreless bout, the winner will be declared by decision of the five judges.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:1-18)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17)

Points were earned as follows:

*   _Ippon_ (3 points): for hitting the head of the opponent with a kick, or when any technique is applied to a fallen adversary.
*   _Waza-ari_ (2 points): for applying a kick to the belly, side, back or torso of the opponent.
*   _Yuko_ (1 point): for delivering a punch with closed hand (_tsuki_) or strike (_uchi_) to the head, neck, belly, side, back or torso of the opponent.

Strikes below the belt were strictly forbidden and strength must always be controlled as the fighter would receive a warning if they hurt their opponent. Points could be lost or there could even be a disqualification if the resulting injury was severe. Knocking an opponent down to the floor without at least attempting to strike them was also liable to be punished.[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

Warning levels:

*   _Chukoku_ (first warning): for committing a minor infraction for the first time.
*   _Keikoku_ (second warning): for the same minor infraction, or for committing a medium infraction for the first time.
*   _Hansoku-chui_ (third warning): for committing the same minor infraction for the third time, the same medium infraction for a second time, or for committing a major infraction for the first time (usually excessive contact to vital parts or below the belt, really hurting the opponent).
*   _Hansoku_ (fourth and final warning): inflicting serious damage on the team score as a whole. The victory is given to the opponent.

Warnings and punishments were divided into two different categories, the first being for excessive and/or illegal contact and the other for technical violations, such as leaving the _koto_ (fighting space) or faking an injury in order to make the referee give the opponent a warning.

### Kata

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kata")]

Each of seven judges evaluates the performance individually within the scale of 5.0 to 10.0, in increments of 0.2 for technical points and athletic points respectively. The two highest and two lowest scores out of the seven scores of each group are eliminated and all the remaining scores are added to make up the final scores, which is weighed 70% for technical points and 30% for athletic points. In the case of a draw, the competitors perform an additional choice of kata to be judged.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17)

There are 7 criteria of evaluation for technical points: stances, techniques, transitional movements, timing, correct breathing, focus and conformance. 3 evaluation criteria for athletic points are: strength, speed and balance.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17)

## Qualification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Qualification")]

Main article: [Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Qualification "Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Qualification")

There are 80 qualifying spots for karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics.

A nation can have no more than 8 athletes qualify (up to four males and four females) with a maximum of one in each event.

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Summary")]

The 10 competitors in each event qualify as follows:

*   1 from the host nation, Japan
*   4 from the Olympic Standing ranking as of 5 April 2021
*   3 from the Olympics Karate 2020 Qualification Tournament
*   2 from continental representation or Tripartite Commission invitation

Because World Karate Federation rankings are based on five weight classes instead of the three weight classes featured in the 2020 Olympics, some of the Olympic events are based on a combination of two WKF classes. In those cases, the top 2 from each of the WKF classes qualify for the combined Olympic class (for a total of 4). Where the Olympic class matches the WKF class, the top 4 in that class qualify.

The qualification tournament features the same weight classes as the Olympic weight classes. Only [National Olympic Committees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOCs) that have not qualified through Olympic standing for a given division are eligible to enter an athlete in the qualification tournament. The top three finishers in each division at the qualification tournament qualify for the Olympics.

A total of 10 quota places, distributed among the eight events, are available through continental representation. The selection order is as follows:

| Continent | Spots |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oceania | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Africa | 2 | 1 per gender |
| North America | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Asia | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Europe | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Africa | 1 | either gender |
| South America | 1 | either gender |

For each continent, all of the gold medalists at the continental games are considered together. The highest ranked among this group earns the qualification spot unless that competitor is already qualified or otherwise cannot be selected without violating any of the following limitations: 10 athletes per division, 1 athlete per NOC per division, 2 athletes per NOC through continental representation (affecting only Africa and the Americas). If the highest-ranked gold medalist cannot be entered, then the next-highest ranked gold medalist qualifies if possible. This process goes through all gold medalists by ranking, then all silver medalists by ranking, then all bronze medalists by ranking until the continent's qualifying spots are filled. If none of the medalists can be entered, the highest-ranked eligible athlete from that continent in the rankings (regardless of finish at the continental games) qualifies.

[Karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate") was an event held in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan. It was the debut appearance of [karate at the Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Karate at the Summer Olympics"). Karate was one of four optional sports added to the Olympic program specifically for 2020,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-1) rather than as a permanent sport.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-3) After it was announced it would not be included in 2024, in August 2022 it was announced that karate had made the shortlist for inclusion in the [2028 Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics "2028 Summer Olympics"), although it was ultimately not selected.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-5)

The karate competitions at the 2020 Olympics featured eight events.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Tokyo_2020_Karate-6) Two karate disciplines were featured: [kumite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumite "Kumite") was the sparring discipline and had three weight classes each for men and women; [kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kata_(martial_arts) "Kata (martial arts)") was the solo form discipline, and had one event each for men and women. Competitors chose the kata to demonstrate from 102 kata that were recognized by the World Karate Federation. Competitors were not allowed to demonstrate the same kata twice during the tournament.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Tokyo_2020_Karate-6) Each event had 10 competitors.

The three weight classes in Olympic competition for kumite were in contrast to the five normally used by the World Karate Federation (WKF). The two lightest (-60 kg and -67 kg for men, -50 kg and -55 kg for women) were combined into the Olympic categories of -67 kg for men and -55 kg for women. The middle categories (-75 kg men, -61 kg women) were unchanged, while the two heaviest categories (-84 kg and +84 kg for men, -68 kg and +68 kg for women) were combined into +75 kg for men and +61 kg for women.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

The effort to bring karate to the Olympics was begun in the 1970s by [Jacques Delcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Delcourt "Jacques Delcourt").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Inc.1985-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Coleman1993-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-9) In 2009, in the [121st International Olympic Committee voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/121st_IOC_Session "121st IOC Session"), karate did not receive the necessary two-thirds majority vote to become an [Olympic sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sport "Olympic sport").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-10) Karate was being considered for the 2020 Olympics;[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-11) however, at a meeting of the IOC's executive board, held in [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") on 29 May 2013, it was decided that karate (along with [wushu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wushu_(sport) "Wushu (sport)") and several other sports) would not be considered for inclusion in 2020 at the [IOC's 125th session](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/125th_IOC_Session "125th IOC Session") in [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), in September 2013.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-12)

In September 2015, karate was included in a shortlist with [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Baseball at the Summer Olympics"), [softball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Softball at the Summer Olympics"), [skateboarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skateboarding_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Skateboarding at the Summer Olympics"), [surfing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Surfing at the Summer Olympics"), and [sport climbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_climbing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Sport climbing at the Summer Olympics") to be considered for inclusion in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-13) and in June 2016, the Executive Board of the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) announced that they would support the proposal to include all of the shortlisted sports in the 2020 Games.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-14) Finally, on 3 August 2016, all five sports (counting baseball and softball together as one sport) were approved for inclusion in the 2020 Olympic program.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-15) Karate will not be included in the [2024 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Olympic_Games "2024 Olympic Games") or the 2028 Games.

## Rules

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Rules")]

For both kumite and kata, WKF rules, effective as of January 2018, have been adopted.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17) In January 2019, a point-based system was adopted for kata.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:1-18)

### Kumite

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Kumite")]

The individual tournament for the Kumite competition at the World Karate Federation (WKF) [Karate World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_World_Championships "Karate World Championships") is held under a weight class system comprising five divisions each for both men and women.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-19) However, the Kumite competition at the Summer Olympics consisted of just three divisions each, thus:

*   Weight classes for men: −67 kg, −75 kg, +75 kg
*   Weight classes for women: −55 kg, −61 kg, +61 kg[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-20)

Two competitors face each other in a matted competition area of 8 m ×8 m (26 ft ×26 ft). Each match is competed for 3 minutes, unless one competitor amasses eight points more than their opponent.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:1-18) A competitor wins by amassing eight points more than their opponent or by gaining more points than their opponent in the allotted time of 3 minutes. In the event of a tie, the competitor who scored the first point is the winner. In the case of a scoreless bout, the winner will be declared by decision of the five judges.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:1-18)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17)

Points were earned as follows:

*   _Ippon_ (3 points): for hitting the head of the opponent with a kick, or when any technique is applied to a fallen adversary.
*   _Waza-ari_ (2 points): for applying a kick to the belly, side, back or torso of the opponent.
*   _Yuko_ (1 point): for delivering a punch with closed hand (_tsuki_) or strike (_uchi_) to the head, neck, belly, side, back or torso of the opponent.

Strikes below the belt were strictly forbidden and strength must always be controlled as the fighter would receive a warning if they hurt their opponent. Points could be lost or there could even be a disqualification if the resulting injury was severe. Knocking an opponent down to the floor without at least attempting to strike them was also liable to be punished.[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

Warning levels:

*   _Chukoku_ (first warning): for committing a minor infraction for the first time.
*   _Keikoku_ (second warning): for the same minor infraction, or for committing a medium infraction for the first time.
*   _Hansoku-chui_ (third warning): for committing the same minor infraction for the third time, the same medium infraction for a second time, or for committing a major infraction for the first time (usually excessive contact to vital parts or below the belt, really hurting the opponent).
*   _Hansoku_ (fourth and final warning): inflicting serious damage on the team score as a whole. The victory is given to the opponent.

Warnings and punishments were divided into two different categories, the first being for excessive and/or illegal contact and the other for technical violations, such as leaving the _koto_ (fighting space) or faking an injury in order to make the referee give the opponent a warning.

### Kata

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kata")]

Each of seven judges evaluates the performance individually within the scale of 5.0 to 10.0, in increments of 0.2 for technical points and athletic points respectively. The two highest and two lowest scores out of the seven scores of each group are eliminated and all the remaining scores are added to make up the final scores, which is weighed 70% for technical points and 30% for athletic points. In the case of a draw, the competitors perform an additional choice of kata to be judged.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17)

There are 7 criteria of evaluation for technical points: stances, techniques, transitional movements, timing, correct breathing, focus and conformance. 3 evaluation criteria for athletic points are: strength, speed and balance.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-:0-17)

## Qualification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Qualification")]

Main article: [Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Qualification "Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Qualification")

There are 80 qualifying spots for karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics.

A nation can have no more than 8 athletes qualify (up to four males and four females) with a maximum of one in each event.

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Summary")]

The 10 competitors in each event qualify as follows:

*   1 from the host nation, Japan
*   4 from the Olympic Standing ranking as of 5 April 2021
*   3 from the Olympics Karate 2020 Qualification Tournament
*   2 from continental representation or Tripartite Commission invitation

Because World Karate Federation rankings are based on five weight classes instead of the three weight classes featured in the 2020 Olympics, some of the Olympic events are based on a combination of two WKF classes. In those cases, the top 2 from each of the WKF classes qualify for the combined Olympic class (for a total of 4). Where the Olympic class matches the WKF class, the top 4 in that class qualify.

The qualification tournament features the same weight classes as the Olympic weight classes. Only [National Olympic Committees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOCs) that have not qualified through Olympic standing for a given division are eligible to enter an athlete in the qualification tournament. The top three finishers in each division at the qualification tournament qualify for the Olympics.

A total of 10 quota places, distributed among the eight events, are available through continental representation. The selection order is as follows:

| Continent | Spots |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oceania | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Africa | 2 | 1 per gender |
| North America | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Asia | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Europe | 2 | 1 per gender |
| Africa | 1 | either gender |
| South America | 1 | either gender |

For each continent, all of the gold medalists at the continental games are considered together. The highest ranked among this group earns the qualification spot unless that competitor is already qualified or otherwise cannot be selected without violating any of the following limitations: 10 athletes per division, 1 athlete per NOC per division, 2 athletes per NOC through continental representation (affecting only Africa and the Americas). If the highest-ranked gold medalist cannot be entered, then the next-highest ranked gold medalist qualifies if possible. This process goes through all gold medalists by ranking, then all silver medalists by ranking, then all bronze medalists by ranking until the continent's qualifying spots are filled. If none of the medalists can be entered, the highest-ranked eligible athlete from that continent in the rankings (regardless of finish at the continental games) qualifies.

**Ryo Kiyuna** (喜友名諒, _Kiyuna Ryō_, born 12 July 1990)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_results_asian_games_2018-2) is an Okinawan [karateka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate"). He won the gold medal in the [men's kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_kata "Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's kata") event at the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") in Tokyo, Japan.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-world_champion_kiyuna_wins_first_mens_olympic_kata_title_2021-3) He is also a four-time gold medalist in the men's kata event at the [World Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Karate_Championships "World Karate Championships") and a two-time gold medalist in the men's team kata event, alongside [Arata Kinjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arata_Kinjo "Arata Kinjo") and [Takuya Uemura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takuya_Uemura "Takuya Uemura").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-remembering_world_karate_championships_2018-4) He has also won multiple gold medals in both the individual and team kata events at the [Asian Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Karate_Championships "Asian Karate Championships").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ryo_Kiyuna&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

At the [2012 World Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_World_Karate_Championships "2012 World Karate Championships") held in Paris, France, Kiyuna won one of the bronze medals in the men's individual kata event.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-tokyo_weekender_meet_sensation_tokyo_2020-5) The following year, he [represented Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_at_the_2013_World_Games "Japan at the 2013 World Games") at the [2013 World Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Games "2013 World Games") in Cali, Colombia and he won the bronze medal in the [men's kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2013_World_Games "Karate at the 2013 World Games") event.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_medalists_world_games_2013-6)

In 2014, at the [World Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Karate_Championships "2014 World Karate Championships") held in Bremen, Germany, Kiyuna won the gold medal in the men's individual kata event.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-tokyo_weekender_meet_sensation_tokyo_2020-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-four_gold_medals_opening_day_world_championships_2016-7) At the [2016 World Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_World_Karate_Championships "2016 World Karate Championships") held in Linz, Austria, he won the gold medal in both the men's individual and men's team kata events.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-tokyo_weekender_meet_sensation_tokyo_2020-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-four_gold_medals_opening_day_world_championships_2016-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-japan_top_medal_table_world_2016-8) In 2017, Kiyuna won the gold medal in the [men's kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2017_World_Games_%E2%80%93_Men's_kata "Karate at the 2017 World Games – Men's kata") event at the [World Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Games "2017 World Games") held in Wrocław, Poland.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-tokyo_weekender_meet_sensation_tokyo_2020-5)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-kiyuna_shimizu_gold_world_games_2017-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_results_world_games_2017-10) In the final, he defeated [Damián Quintero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dami%C3%A1n_Quintero "Damián Quintero") of Spain.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_results_world_games_2017-10)

At the [2018 Asian Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Asian_Karate_Championships "2018 Asian Karate Championships") held in Amman, Jordan, Kiyuna won the gold medal in the men's kata event.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-japan_claim_seven_gold_asian_karate_2018-11) A month later, he won the gold medal in the [men's kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2018_Asian_Games_%E2%80%93_Men's_kata "Karate at the 2018 Asian Games – Men's kata") event at the [2018 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Asian_Games "2018 Asian Games") held in Jakarta, Indonesia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-tokyo_weekender_meet_sensation_tokyo_2020-5)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_results_asian_games_2018-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-unified_korean_team_dragon_boat_2018-12) In the final, he defeated [Wang Yi-ta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Yi-ta "Wang Yi-ta") of Taiwan. In 2019, at the [Asian Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Asian_Karate_Championships "2019 Asian Karate Championships") held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, he won the gold medal in both the men's individual kata and men's team kata events.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-japan_earn_six_titles_uzbek_golden_2019-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-asian_karate_championships_results_2019-14)

Kiyuna [represented Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Japan at the 2020 Summer Olympics") at the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") in Tokyo, Japan.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-wkf_announces_first_qualified_2020-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-wkf_announces_first_forty_tokyo_2020-16) He won the gold medal in the [men's kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_kata "Karate at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's kata") event,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-kiyuna_mesmerises_to_win_kata_gold_2021-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_one_games_wonder_drama_emotion_tokyo_2020-18) becoming Japan's first gold medalist from Okinawa.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-olympics.com-19) In the final, he defeated [Damián Quintero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dami%C3%A1n_Quintero "Damián Quintero") of Spain.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_results_book_summer_olympics_2020-20) He was also the flag bearer for Japan during the [closing ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics_closing_ceremony "2020 Summer Olympics closing ceremony").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-closing_ceremony_flag_bearers_summer_olympics_2020-21) A few months after the Olympics, he won the gold medal in the [men's kata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_World_Karate_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_individual_kata "2021 World Karate Championships – Men's individual kata") event at the [2021 World Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_World_Karate_Championships "2021 World Karate Championships") held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-kiyuna_makes_history_as_olympic_gold_medallists_retain_titles_karate_world_championships_2021-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-world_karate_championships_results_book_2021-23) In December 2021, he won the gold medal in both the men's individual and men's team kata events at the [Asian Karate Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Asian_Karate_Championships "2021 Asian Karate Championships") held in Almaty, Kazakhstan.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-japan_top_medal_table_asian_karate_championships_in_almaty_2021-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-results_book_asian_karate_championships_2021-25)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ryo_Kiyuna&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

He studied at [Okinawa International University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okinawa_International_University "Okinawa International University").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-ryukyu_shimpo_determined_to_win_tokyo_2020-1) In December 2020, he contracted [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronavirus_disease_2019 "Coronavirus disease 2019").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-karate_world_kiyuna_contracts_coronavirus_2020-26)

Kiyuna's mother died in 2019 at the age of 57. At the gold medal ceremony for kata at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, Kiyuna paid tribute to his mother's support by carrying a framed picture of her during the proceedings.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-wapost-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryo_Kiyuna#cite_note-kyodo-28)
